title: Finite scalar local models have two-term finite-free sheaf resolutions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $T$ any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Choose either $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, or $A=E$, $\Lambda=\underline E$, with the usual condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On the small pro-étale site of $T$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an $A$-module $Q$, write $\underline Q$ for its constant module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the canonical map $\underline A\to B_T$. Let $P$ be a finitely presented $A$-module, meaning that it is the cokernel of a map $A^s\to A^t$ with $s,t$ finite, and put $L=B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$ [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. There are finite nonnegative integers $a,b$ and an exact scalar sequence $0\to A^a\xrightarrow{u}A^b\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$ whose constant sheafification followed by extension of scalars yields an exact sequence of $B_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]
$$0\longrightarrow B_T^a\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline u}B_T^b\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline v}L\longrightarrow0.$$
Thus the augmented cochain complex $[B_T^a\to B_T^b]\to L[0]$, with free terms in degrees $-1,0$, is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. In the case $A=E$ one may take $a=0$, so $L$ is finite free. No Noetherianity assumption on $T$, torsion-freeness assumption on $P$, or completion of the derived category is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), proof: the finite projective scalar resolution for a finitely presented O_E-module, with Lemma 6.8.2(1) for the coefficient limit. Length-one finite-free strengthening for finite E/Q_ell; exact constant sheafification and scalar extension are Stacks sites-modules Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact) and 093M (lemma-completion-flat).

proof.text: First suppose $A=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a discrete valuation ring and a domain. Choose a presentation $A^s\xrightarrow{w}A^t\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$ as in the hypothesis, and set $K=\ker(v)=\operatorname{im}(w)$. The images under $w$ of the $s$ coordinate vectors generate $K$. Also $K$ is torsion-free: if $0\ne r\in A$ and $rx=0$ in $K\subseteq A^t$, then each coordinate of $x$ is zero because $A$ is a domain. Thus [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] gives a finite basis of $K$, say $K\cong A^a$. Put $b=t$ and let $u:A^a\to A^b$ be this basis isomorphism followed by the inclusion of $K$. It is injective, its image is $\ker v$, and $v$ is surjective. This constructs the required scalar short exact sequence without any torsion-freeness assumption on $P$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), proof: finite projective scalar resolution, strengthened to length one using Stacks Tag 0AUW (more-algebra.tex, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3).

proof.text: If $A=E$, the images of the $t$ coordinate vectors in a finite presentation span $P$. Delete a vector whenever it is a linear combination of the others. This finite procedure preserves the span and ends with an independent spanning family: any nontrivial linear relation would express a vector with nonzero coefficient as a combination of the others, since $E$ is a field. If $b$ vectors remain, the coordinate map $v:E^b\to P$ is therefore bijective. Take $a=0$ and $u:0\to E^b$. This gives the scalar sequence in the field case, including $P=0$ with the empty basis.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), scalar-resolution argument; elementary finite spanning-set argument for the field case.

proof.text: On the chosen small site $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, form the constant presheaves of the scalar short exact sequence just constructed. The sequence is exact sectionwise, with all restriction maps the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], its sheafification is an exact sequence of $\underline A$-module sheaves. It is the constant-sheaf sequence by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The same sheafification theorem preserves finite limits and colimits; hence the sheafification of $A^n$ is $\underline A^n$, with the usual coordinate maps, also for $n=0$. We obtain $0\to\underline A^a\xrightarrow{\underline u}\underline A^b\xrightarrow{\underline v}\underline P\to0$.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), with the constant presheaf of rings A; equivalently Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact).

proof.text: For either coefficient ring, use the balanced coequalizer defining [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. The map $B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline A^n\to B_T^n$ sends $z\otimes(x_i)$ to $(zx_i)$, using the canonical $\underline A$-action on $B_T$. Its inverse sends $(z_i)$ to $\sum_i z_i\otimes e_i$. These formulas are balanced, commute with restrictions, and compose to the identity by additivity and $z\otimes x e_i=zx\otimes e_i$; equivalently they define inverse maps from the coequalizer. Thus they are isomorphisms of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The formulas include $n=0$. For a matrix $h:A^n\to A^m$, both composites send $z\otimes e_j$ to the column $(z h_{ij})_i$, so this identification carries $1\otimes\underline h$ to its scalar-extended matrix. The final term after scalar extension is precisely $L=B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$ as defined in the statement.

source.place: Section tensor-product: balanced tensor construction; explicit finite-coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Return to $A=\mathcal O_E$, and choose a uniformizer $\varpi$ using step 1. Since a DVR is a principal ideal domain, [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $A$ Noetherian. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] there is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $B_T\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{A/(\varpi^n)}$. It respects the constant $A$-algebra maps: the image of a constant scalar $r$ under its $n$th projection is the residue class of $r$, which characterizes the map into this limit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with this Noetherian $A$ and $I=(\varpi)$. Its flatness assertion says explicitly that tensoring with the limit over $\underline A$ preserves short exact sequences. Transport this along the preceding $\underline A$-algebra isomorphism and apply it to step 3. With the coordinate identifications of step 4 this gives the asserted exact sequence $0\to B_T^a\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline u}B_T^b\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline v}L\to0$. Its maps are $B_T$-linear, and kernels and cokernels in this module category are computed on the underlying sheaves as specified in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), via Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(1) and the existing condensed/limit identification. No hypothesis on the scheme beyond being a scheme is used.

proof.text: In the field case step 2 made $v:E^b\to P$ an isomorphism. Its constant sheafification has inverse the sheafification of $v^{-1}$; after extension of scalars the two inverses still compose to the identities by functoriality of tensor. Step 4 therefore gives $B_T^b\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, and with $a=0$ the asserted sequence is exact. In particular $L$ is finite free. This argument requires no flatness assertion for $B_T$ over the discrete constant sheaf $\underline E$.

source.place: Elementary field case of the scalar-resolution argument, after the finite-coordinate identification in step 4.

proof.text: Let $C^\bullet$ have $C^{-1}=B_T^a$, $C^0=B_T^b$, differential $1\otimes\underline u$, and all other terms zero [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The map to $L[0]$ has degree-zero component $1\otimes\underline v$ and all other components zero; it is a cochain map because $vu=0$. Steps 5 and 6 show $H^{-1}(C)=\ker(1\otimes\underline u)=0$ and $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}(1\otimes\underline u)\cong L$, with the latter isomorphism induced by the specified augmentation. Every other cohomology sheaf is zero, as for $L[0]$. By [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. These computations take place in the ordinary module-sheaf category, so they require neither completion of the derived category nor Noetherianity of $T$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite-resolution argument; direct cohomology calculation for the constructed augmented two-term complex.

I checked the A-algebra compatibility of that identification; it is not automatic, since Galois-twisted reductions exist, and it follows from the representability in clauses (1)-(2), which the step uses as stated. Steps 6-7: the field case needs no flatness; H^{-1}=0 and H^0 is L through the augmentation. Small cases checked: P=0, P free, P=O_E/pi^n, s=0, field case; nothing is assumed on T. lean.statement: theorem finite_constant_model_two_term_free_resolution (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (T : Scheme.{u}) : (∀ (P : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) [Module.FinitePresentation (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E) P], HasResolution (integralModel l E T) (Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoefficients l E) T)) P false) ∧ (∀ (P : ModuleCat.{u + 1} E) [Module.FinitePresentation E P], HasResolution (rationalModel l E T) (Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (rationalCoefficients l E) T)) P true)
lean.note: The integral and rational cases are the two conjuncts. Canonical constant-module and scalar-extension helpers belong to this local-model resolution and contain real data. HasResolution records the scalar sequence, its actual functorial image, both finite-free identifications, the component-normalized augmented complex, and QuasiIso of that augmentation. The rational case records a=0 and finite freeness of the final model explicitly.
